title: BNCI 2016-002 Emergency Braking during Simulated Driving dataset
description: This dataset comprises EEG and EMG recordings from 15 healthy participants performing emergency braking tasks during simulated driving at 200 Hz sampling rate. Participants drove a virtual racing car and performed immediate emergency braking when a lead vehicle decelerated abruptly, with the goal of detecting braking intention from neural and muscular signals. The preprocessed data includes 59 EEG channels, 1 EMG channel, 2 EOG channels, and 7 miscellaneous technical channels (69 total channels), including vehicle dynamics measurements (brake, distance to lead vehicle, gas, lead vehicle brake, lead vehicle gas, wheel X/Y), enabling research on predictive braking assistance systems and neuroergonomic applications.
methods_description: Data were acquired using a BrainAmp system with 59 EEG channels (extended 10-20 montage, Ag/AgCl sensors, nose reference), 1 EMG channel, 2 EOG channels, and 7 miscellaneous technical channels at 200 Hz sampling rate. Participants performed three 45-minute blocks of simulated driving with 10-15 minute rest intervals. Emergency braking events were triggered by lead vehicle deceleration (20-40s inter-stimulus-interval) requiring immediate response. Preprocessing included highpass filtering (0.1 Hz), lowpass filtering (45 Hz for EEG), bandpass filtering (15-90 Hz for EMG), 50 Hz notch filtering, EMG rectification, baseline correction, and synchronization across all signals.
